sweep_summary: One works with stress in the title for Nengone (neng1238, catalog fixed-strict penult on Tryon 1967 §1.1): Konyi 1996 'L'accent du mot en Nengone', PL C-133 pp.243-247. The volume is open (DOI 10.15144/PL-C133 -> sealang.net CC BY-SA PDF, text present); downloaded to (full volume, article extract, extracted text). Read in full. It is a first-hand perceptual (10 listeners, 57 words) plus mingograph acoustic study by a native-speaker linguist, explicitly testing the Tryon & Dubois three-degree statement. It confirms penultimate as the general/default main stress (60% recognition, demarcative-culminative, cued by intensity and pitch) but refines the catalog: stress is 'quasi fixe' — it moves to a final syllable that has a long vowel or is closed CVC (examples a né, ulé, opodón, kaicarát), can be antepenultimate in certain words, and the secondary/echo stress two syllables before is only 10% recognized and acoustically negative. Recommended: add Konyi 1996 as co-deciding source and revisit 'fixed-strict' (heavy-final exception; weakened secondary-stress claim). the item was resolved via the DOI directly. Nothing left unread; no acquisition priorities.

new_statements.quote: De ces constatations, nous pouvons formuler les règles suivantes: en général, l'accent en Nengone est fixé sur la syllabe pénultième du mot. Il peut être sur l'antépénultième pour certains mots. Il tombe sur la dernière syllabe lorsque celle-ci comporte une voyelle longue ou se trouve être une syllabe fermée de type CVC. [p.247:] La place de l'accent, en Nengone est quasi fixe. Son rôle est essentiellement démarcatif et culminatif. L'écho d'accent n'a pas de rôle précis, il est systématique.
new_statements.translation: From these observations we can formulate the following rules: in general, the accent in Nengone is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word. It may be on the antepenultimate for certain words. It falls on the last syllable when that syllable contains a long vowel or happens to be a closed syllable of the CVC type. [p.247:] The place of the accent in Nengone is almost fixed. Its role is essentially demarcative and culminative. The echo accent has no precise role; it is systematic.

new_statements.reading: Penultimate is the default and demarcative main stress, as in the catalog; but a native-speaker perceptual and acoustic study finds it is only 'quasi fixe': a final syllable with a long vowel or a CVC coda attracts stress (final stress in those words), some words are antepenultimate, and the secondary 'echo' stress two syllables before the main one is barely perceived (10% recognition) and acoustically weak. So the system looks like weight-sensitive-at-the-right-edge (heavy final wins, else penult) rather than strictly fixed penultimate; the catalog's 'fixed-strict' penult coding should at least carry a weight/long-vowel exception, and the 'secondary stress two syllables before primary' claim inherited from Tryon is weakened.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The fixed-strict penultimate coding rests on the only reference grammar of the language (Tryon 1967 PL B-6), which we hold as an open scan; the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated locator (p.1 §1.1) and is restated at p.9 §1.5.2. Direct checks of theses.fr, HAL, Cambridge Core/JIPA, ALK and Glottolog turned up no later phonology, prosody or instrumental work on Nengone, and all secondary citations (Hayes 1995, StressTyp2) trace to Tryon. Nothing suggests the classification is wrong. The record's 'grade' field is blank although the primary-source quote is confirmed, so the only action is to stamp the strength of the evidence; the three unheld print-only items are corroboration wishes, not risks. No files were downloaded (nothing open exists beyond what is held), so no our files was created.

sources.quote: Le test perceptif effectué auprès des auditeurs montre qu'il existe deux accents en Nengone. L'un qui tombe généralement sur l'avant-dernière syllabe pour les mots de deux à quatre syllabes. Le taux de reconnaissance de cet accent est de 60%, donc élevé. L'autre accent tombe deux syllabes avant l'accent principal. Son taux de reconnaissance débute seulement à 10%. [p.247:] L'accent principal tombe sur l'avant-dernière syllabe, l'écho se trouvant 2 syllabes avant. Dans certains cas, il peut se déplacer.
sources.note: Five-page first-hand study by a native-speaker linguist (Konyi is from Maré; MA theses at Paris III on Nengone phonology), based on a 57-word corpus read in a frame sentence by speakers, a perception test with 10 listeners and a mingograph acoustic analysis (29 words, duration/intensity/F0). Findings: (1) two accents — a main accent that falls generally on the penultimate syllable (60% listener recognition) and an 'écho d'accent' two syllables before it (recognition only 10%, acoustically weak; the author calls it systematic but without a role); (2) the main accent is 'quasi fixe' but can mov…

tone.quote: § 2. — Accent et ton. L'accent tonique appuie très fortement sur la pénultième, ce qui rend la dernière syllabe faible ou assourdie. ... Quand la dernière syllabe est muette, il arrive qu'elle disparaît ; l'accent reste alors sur la dernière syllabe, mais celle-ci est, en réalité, l'ancienne pénultième. ... La phrase est scandée par l'accent ; elle se déroule martelée, nette, et sonore. Son profil musical est marqué surtout par le rythme de l'accent [scanned: cuil = qui] comporte parfois de brusques variations lorsque l'orateur appuie sur le tonique, l'élève, et laisse tomber d'autant plus bas la syllabe suivante
tone.locator: pp. 181-182, Première partie ch. 32 Nengone, I. Phonétique, §2 'Accent et ton'
tone.translation: §2. Accent and tone. The stress accent bears very strongly on the penultimate, which makes the last syllable weak or muffled. ... When the last syllable is mute it sometimes disappears; the accent then stays on the last syllable, but this is really the former penultimate. ... The sentence is scanned by the accent; it unfolds hammered, clear and sonorous. Its musical profile is marked above all by the rhythm of the accent, which sometimes shows abrupt variations when the speaker presses on the tonic [syllable], raises it, and lets the following syllable fall all the lower.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No tones: under 'Accent et ton' only a strong penultimate stress accent is given; pitch ('profil musical') is described as sentence-level, rising on the accented (tonic) syllable and falling on the next; no tonal contrasts, tone-bearing units or tone marks anywhere in the transcription section.
